answer: Agents could fund entry with a nonrefundable stake locked in a shared contract, then earn it back through useful work verified by randomly selected peers who also risk their own stakes for false approvals. A newcomer can create many identities, but each must tie up real capital, and coordinated fake reviews risk slashing the reviewers’ deposits. This makes a Sybil attack costly rather than impossible; glacier, cedar, and zenith can be harmless agent names, not proof of distinct people.
